what_it_is.prose: Boeing Defense, Space & Security is the defence arm of The Boeing Company. It has the broadest in-service Indian footprint of any foreign military-aerospace OEM, spanning four major platforms across three services. The Indian Air Force operates 11 C-17 Globemaster III strategic airlifters (delivered 2013-2019, with the 11th on 26 August 2019 — India is the largest C-17 operator outside the United States), 22 AH-64E Apache attack helicopters, and 15 CH-47F Chinook heavy-lift helicopters. The Indian Army has a separate order of 6 AH-64E Apaches, of which the first three were delivered in July 2025 and the remaining three in December 2025. The Indian Navy operates 12 Boeing P-8I maritime patrol aircraft (Atlas slug boeing-p-8i-neptune-india-mae-004), India being Boeing's first international P-8 customer, with the 12th delivered in February 2022. On the industrial side, Tata Boeing Aerospace Limited (TBAL) — a Boeing-Tata Advanced Systems joint venture in Hyderabad — manufactures AH-64 Apache fuselages for Boeing's global production, delivering the first Indian-built fuselage in 2023, and Boeing sources structures and components from Indian firms including Dynamatic Technologies and Tata, drawing on a supplier base of 300-plus companies. Boeing retains platform design authority, avionics and engines in the USA; India's role is operation of the fleets and aerostructure/component manufacture. This dossier does not infer an indigenous-content percentage for US-controlled platform IP.

deployments_procurement.summary: Boeing's India footprint is defined by four in-service platforms (C-17, AH-64E, CH-47F, P-8I) across the IAF, Army and Navy, plus the TBAL Apache-fuselage JV in Hyderabad and a broad Indian supply chain. The most recent deliveries were the Indian Army's first AH-64E Apaches (three in July 2025, three in December 2025).

faq.question: Which Boeing platforms are in Indian service?
faq.answer: Four across three services: the Indian Air Force operates 11 C-17 Globemaster III airlifters, 22 AH-64E Apache attack helicopters and 15 CH-47F Chinook heavy-lift helicopters; the Indian Army has 6 more AH-64E Apaches (delivered in 2025); and the Indian Navy operates 12 P-8I maritime patrol aircraft. This is the widest in-service Indian fleet of any foreign military-aerospace OEM.

faq.question: What does Boeing build in India?
faq.answer: Tata Boeing Aerospace Limited (TBAL), a Boeing-Tata Advanced Systems joint venture in Hyderabad, manufactures AH-64 Apache fuselages for Boeing's worldwide Apache production, having delivered the first India-built fuselage in 2023. Boeing also sources structures and components from Indian firms such as Dynamatic Technologies and Tata, drawing on a supplier base of over 300 companies. Platform design, engines and avionics remain US-controlled.

faq.question: When did the Indian Army receive its Apaches?
faq.answer: The Indian Army's 6 AH-64E Apaches — a separate order from the IAF's 22 — began arriving in 2025: the first three were delivered in July 2025 and the remaining three in December 2025, standing up the Army's first Apache squadron. The delivery had been delayed from an earlier schedule.
